audit.whatIsWrong: The page attributes Maokai's sustain to his saplings in five places — 'sustain from passive saplings', 'sapling heals', 'passive sapling sustain', 'passive sapling heals'. Saplings are Sapling Toss (E) and heal nothing. His healing is Sap Magic, his passive, and the page misses the one clause that decides the lane.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.' Being struck by YOUR abilities accelerates his heal. So the standard advice — chip him with your Q — actively refills him. Auto-attack pressure is the correct answer, and Grievous Wounds is mandatory. Separately, Twisted Advance makes him untargetable while it dashes, which can eat a timed burst.
audit.corrected: Sap Magic named and the spell-acceleration clause written into spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text, mid, whys[3], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1]; the untargetable dash into wants.you[0], dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears anywhere on the page, and Nature's Grasp is described without range or timer.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10 at 525, Bramble Smash a 7s knock-back at 600, Sapling Toss 18s at 1100 and 'more effective in brush', Nature's Grasp 130/110/90 at 3000 range. The 130s ultimate is the largest recurring window in the lane and the brush clause is why a bush fight is worse than an open one.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, spikes[0].text and mid.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a wash with his sapling heals negating your poke.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a wash: every spell you land speeds up his Sap Magic heal.

edits.before: It's a farming stalemate — Maokai's W Twisted Advance is a targeted root that sets up his Q Bramble Smash knock-back, but he's a low-damage tank in lane, so you won't die and neither will he. Dodge W by juking around minions and you can chip with Q Darkin Glaive, but don't over-commit into his sustain from passive saplings.
edits.after: It's a farming stalemate — Twisted Advance (W, 14s) makes him untargetable as it dashes, then roots you for a Bramble Smash knock-back. Sap Magic is the real problem: his heal cooldown drops every time he casts a spell or is struck by one, so chipping him with abilities is what refills him. Trade with autos.

edits.before: He spikes into tank items with heavy sustain — his passive heal and W root make him unkillable one-on-one while he provides utility. This is where his edge shows: you can't burst through his health and sap-heal, and his CC lets his team snowball off any pick.
edits.after: He spikes into tank items with heavy sustain — Sap Magic plus his health pool makes him hard to kill alone. Grievous Wounds is not optional here, and his heal accelerates off spells striking him, so a long ability-poke war refills him faster than it drains him.

edits.before: Through levels 3-6 it remains a stalemate: you can chip with Q Darkin Glaive, but his passive sapling sustain heals it back and his W root sets up a Bramble Smash trade you don't want to eat. At 6 his R Nature's Grasp turns the lane into a gank-heavy zone, so ward his flanks and don't push blindly into a champion who can point-and-click root you for his jungler.
edits.after: Through levels 3-6 it remains a stalemate: chip him and Sap Magic heals it back faster, because being struck by a spell shortens its cooldown. His W roots you into a Bramble Smash knock-back you do not want to eat. At 6 Nature's Grasp (130s, 3000 range) turns the lane gank-heavy, so ward his flanks and never push in blind.

notes: The kit file gives Bramble Smash a 'grounding' flag, but Riot's description says only that it knocks back and slows. Grounding would shut off Zaahen's E dash and would be the most important line on the page, so it is worth a human confirming — I wrote nothing claiming it, per the rule that the description beats a derived flag. Zaahen's ability names remain unavailable from his kit file, so slot letters are used rather than the content layer's 'Darkin Glaive'.
